_u.a_criticise1_e: Point out problems at his/her recent work, ask him/her about his experience, confirm the reasons for the decline in performance, and discuss solutions with him/her.
_u.a_criticise2_e: Show him/her where your fault is for his/her performance decline, but also point out his/her responsibility. Take punitive measures (such as demerits...) in a timely manner to prevent the possibility of similar problems from happening again.
_u.a_criticise3_e: Point out his/her careless personality that has caused the recent decline in performance; establish a follow-up action plan with him/her on how to improve his/her personality deficiencies.
_u.a_criticise4_e: Ask him/her about his/her recent performance decline, point out your concerns and show that you are responsible for improper supervision, understand the ins and outs of the matter, and discuss with him/her the measures and improvement plans for the specific reasons.
_u.a_praise1_e: Use recent meetings as an opportunity to praise his/her progress specifically.
_u.a_praise2_e: Arrange a meeting to share (Presentation), ask him/her to share the difference before and after the change with other colleagues, and recognize his/her efforts.
_u.a_praise3_e: Try to delegate important tasks to him/her to plan and execute so that others understand his/her new role.
_u.a_praise4_e: Encourage him/her to work harder and indicate that you will publicly praise him/her when this work has specific results as an incentive.
_u.a_praise5_e: Ask him/her what kind of incentives are expected? You will find a way to satisfy it.
_u.a_assign1_e: Give him/her the project tasks, clearly stating the deadlines, priorities, and tasks that must be completed. Arrange a mid-term meeting to discuss with him/her to monitor the pace.
_u.a_assign2_e: Give him/her project tasks, tell him/her how to carry out these projects, including time limits and priorities, encourage him/her to follow your suggestions, and require all projects to submit bi-weekly reports to monitor progress.
_u.a_assign3_e: Give him/her project tasks and share your current feelings and thoughts about the company. Ask him/her to introduce you to his/her plans for the project, encourage and support his/her ideas, and meet with him/her regularly to understand the progress of the project.
_u.a_assign4_e: Give him/her the project tasks, emphasize the importance of the project to the future of the company, and ask him/her to contact you if he/she encounters problems. Meet with him/her occasionally and assist whenever possible.
_u.a_challenge_title: Since you arrived, the alum's attitude towards you has always been neutral, but there has never been a quarrel. You have heard that before you took over the position of head of this department, the alum had high hopes that he would be the ideal candidate. You see, alum adopts a passive and uncooperative attitude. You want to meet with them to improve your relationship with them. How should you start the interview with him?
_u.a_challenge1_e: Tell him first that you plan to arrange for him to become a supervisor in the future.
_u.a_challenge2_e: Ask him first about the reasons for his negative and indifferent attitude toward you.
_u.a_challenge3_e: Tell him first that you affirm his loyalty and contribution to the company.
_u.a_challenge4_e: First ask him for some opinions and suggestions on improving department performance.
_u.a_challenge5_e: Tell him first that you will rely on his expertise to help you complete some important work ideas, and ask him for his ideas.
_u.s_instruct_e: Leaders set specific goals for subordinates, make plans, set priorities, instruct details, teach step by step, and check and give feedback in a timely manner.
_u.s_coach_e: The leader explains the ins and outs of the task and gives specific requirements. When subordinates do better, they will be recognized in a timely manner. Continue to guide subordinates to develop work standards, and encourage them to praise.
_u.s_partner_e: Leaders and subordinates make decisions together. Leadership is more about guiding, listening, encouraging, and supporting. Listen to the opinions and suggestions of subordinates more. Encourage subordinates to try to solve problems on their own.
_u.s_deligate_e: Leaders empower subordinates to do work independently. Give more trust, affirmation, recognition. Give your subordinates more challenges. Leaders reduce participation in planning and control over details. Leaders delegate day-to-day tasks to subordinates, but provide support and assistance at all times.

DrillReport.about-explain: , a compelling real-life like simulation, enables you to understand your approach to people leadership. In the simulation, you played the role of a Team Lead, working with a diverse team of 10 members, to meet the targets set for your team. Your objective was to enable your team to perform well by helping them build their skills, and to increase their motivation and engagement.
